subject: Data locality attestation: step-up requirements & conditional egress approval
messages:
From: Andrea Lopez <andrea@zephar-health.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@zephar-health.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Data locality attestation & conditional egress approval request

Jordan —

Thanks for taking this. As part of Zephar Health's security intake for any new inference provider we need two things before we can complete procurement: (1) a formal data locality attestation letter stating where customer data-at-rest and processing will be anchored for the APAC tenant, including transient cache behavior; and (2) explicit confirmation of the company policy for conditional egress (i.e., under what operational circumstances Redwood would allow temporary cross-border processing) plus the maximum duration and controls for that window.

High level asks:
- A short attestation letter we can include in our vendor pack (PDF or signed DocuSign).
- Subprocessor roster for the APAC tenant and dates when each subprocessor is activated.
- Statement on whether cryptographic keys for customer data can be kept in customer-managed KMS / HSM (we are evaluating both).
- Any standard SLA/notice commitments for temporary egress and telemetry we can surface to our DPO.

I've attached Zephar's DPA template/questions as a starting point — we can accept Redwood's standard DPA with the attestation as an addendum. We have an internal requirement to keep any cross-border processing under 72 hours unless explicitly approved — please advise if Redwood can commit to an operational guardrail shorter than that (we prefer 48 hours).

Attachment: DPA_Attestation_Template.docx (docx)

Would appreciate a response and proposed timeline by EOD Friday so procurement can keep the board review on schedule.

Best,
Andrea Lopez
CISO, Zephar Health
andrea@zephar-health.com
+61 412 555 019

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Andrea Lopez <andrea@zephar-health.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data locality attestation & conditional egress approval request

Andrea —

Thanks — appreciate the clear checklist. We're able to move quickly on this. Proposed next steps from our side:

1) Legal will prepare an attestation PDF that confirms APAC tenancy anchoring and describes transient cache behavior. We typically exclude ephemeral KV cache copies that are never persisted beyond X hours; I copied Laura for exact wording.

2) We'll share the current APAC subprocessor roster and activation dates. Note: some edge caching and analytics subprocessors may operate in our monitoring region during short failovers; we'll flag those explicitly.

3) On conditional egress: our default operational policy supports transient cross-region processing for failover and capacity events. We can commit to a 48-hour operational window as an option for enterprise accounts with a DPA addendum and notification hooks (audit logs + email alert to your security contact).

4) Key custody: we support customer-managed KMS for key-wrapped artifacts in our private deployment offering; for hosted tenants we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) with either cloud KMS or an HSM-backed provider (we'll document options).

A few clarifying questions so we scope the attestation correctly:
- Do you need the attestation to reference specific regions (e.g., GCP asia-southeast1) or high-level APAC only?
- Will your DPO require a signed, notarized statement or is an attested PDF from Redwood legal sufficient?
- Any specific uptime/latency SLAs tied to the APAC tenancy you want reflected?

I'll coordinate with Legal and Security and aim to get a draft attestation and the subprocessor roster to you within 48 business hours. If that timeline works, please confirm and we'll route the DocuSign.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
--

Jordan / Karthik —

Legal has reviewed Zephar's template. We can produce an attestation that: 1) confirms customer data at rest for the APAC tenant is anchored to APAC region boundaries, 2) describes transient in-memory/KV cache behavior and our retention max for ephemeral objects, and 3) records our standard operational escalation for conditional egress.

Notes / constraints:
- We should NOT list internal telemetry processors by default; instead provide a customer-facing subprocessor roster that includes vendor name, purpose, region, and activation date.
- For conditional egress we can offer a 48-hour temporary window as a contractual addendum (shorter than the customer 72-hour preference). That requires:
  - Email notice to Zephar's security contact at t0, + audit log dump to an agreed S3/GCS location within 24 hours, and
  - Automatic rollback/eviction of cached artifacts within 48 hours unless a joint exception is approved by legal.
- Key custody language: for hosted customers we can document BYOK options and the difference between cloud-KMS and HSM-backed solutions; full customer-managed HSM (on-prem KMS) requires Private deployment contract.

I've drafted an attestation stub and attached it. Please review and advise any wording changes. If accepted by Zephar we'll sign and return as a PDF and follow up with the subprocessor roster export.

Attachment: Redwood_Attestation_v1.pdf (pdf)
Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-842

Laura Bennett

Jordan / Laura —

This is helpful — thank you. A 48-hour conditional egress window with the notification and audit commitments above is acceptable to our DPO. A few small asks before we close:

- Please include region identifiers (APAC: GCP asia-southeast1 and AWS ap-south-1) in the attestation — that makes our vendor pack clearer.
- In the subprocessor roster, can you flag any analytics/observability processors that may receive telemetry outside APAC during failover? A simple boolean "may_transmit_outside_region" column is fine.
- Regarding keys: we are interested in the BYOK path with HSM-backed key custody. If Redwood can document a migration path (hosted -> dedicated -> private) that preserves customer key custody expectations, please include that text.

Timeline: if we can get the signed attestation and the subprocessor roster by Wednesday EOD (UTC), procurement will route to the final review on Thursday.

If helpful, I'm happy to do a 30-min sync with Laura/Naomi to walk our DPO through the attestation language. Let me know availability.

Best,
Andrea
CISO, Zephar Health
